Chef Chris Kinnun — a lifetime in kitchens, now bringing the experience directly to the table.
From the Family Restaurant to Your Table

He grew up around food. He stayed because of what food does to people.

For Chris, cooking was never just a profession. It began as family life.

He grew up working in his family’s award-winning restaurant, surrounded by the rhythm of a working kitchen and the simple lesson that hospitality is something you do, not something you advertise. You work hard. You respect the food. You take care of people. And when they leave happy, you have done something worthwhile.

Over the years, that early education became a career. Chris developed the technique, discipline and creativity of a fine-dining chef, while never losing the warmth that came from those first restaurant years. His cooking became more refined. His point of view became more defined: thoughtful local procurement, nose-to-tail cooking, respect for the whole ingredient and a determination to waste as little as possible.

But traditional restaurant life has one strange distance built into it. The chef can spend hours creating the meal and never see the moment that matters most—the instant it reaches the person it was made for.

That is what pulled Chris toward private dining. It moved him out from behind the restaurant kitchen and into the heart of the dining experience: close enough to see the first bite, the smile that follows, the eyes that light up, the conversation that changes because everyone at the table has just tasted something wonderful.

For Chris, that is the reward. Food can celebrate a milestone, comfort someone after a hard week, turn an ordinary family dinner into a memory, make two people feel as though the whole evening was created just for them, or bring a room full of people together without anyone needing to explain why it feels special.

Chef Chris creates more than a beautiful meal. With every thoughtful, scrumptious bite, he makes you and your guests feel seen, heard, appreciated, and genuinely cared for—because to Chris, hospitality is every bit as important as the food.

Chris did not leave restaurants because he stopped loving the kitchen. He moved closer to the table because he loves what happens after the food leaves it.

The Chef Behind the Food

Skilled enough to impress. Relaxed enough to feel at home.

Chris loves cooking, but what he really loves is feeding people. The reward is not the fancy plate or the compliment to the chef. It is seeing a guest take a bite, smile without meaning to, and immediately reach for another.

He is creative without being precious, experienced without the chef ego, entertaining without taking over the room, and wonderfully easy to work with. He can make an intimate dinner feel special, turn a family gathering into something memorable, and get kids excited about food instead of intimidated by it.

Questions People Ask Before Hiring a Private Chef

Yes, you can ask that.

If you have never hired a private chef before, you are not supposed to magically know how it works. Here are the questions Chris hears most often.

Ready to talk food?

Tell Chris a little about yourself and what sounds delicious. No polished plan required.

Help Chris Get to Know You
How do I get started?

Start with a consultation. Tell Chris who is coming, what you are celebrating—or not celebrating—what you love to eat, what you avoid, and what kind of experience you want. From there, he can begin shaping a fully custom menu.

What does Chef Chris’s private chef service include?

Depending on the experience, service can include menu planning, sourcing and shopping, preparation, cooking in your home, meal execution, kitchen cleanup and thoughtful handling of leftovers. The details are confirmed in advance so you know exactly what to expect.

Do you handle the grocery shopping?

Yes. Chris can handle the ingredient shopping and procurement, choosing high-quality products with attention to seasonality, thoughtful sourcing, local options when possible and his low-waste cooking philosophy.

Do you cook in my kitchen?

Yes, private dining is designed to happen in your home. Chris will talk through the kitchen setup with you ahead of time so he knows what equipment and work space are available and what he may need to bring.

Do you use my dishes and cookware?

That depends on the menu and the experience. Chris can work with appropriate cookware, serving pieces and dishes in your home and can discuss any additional equipment or service pieces needed before the event.

Do you clean up afterward?

Yes. Cleanup is part of making the evening feel cared for from beginning to end. The goal is for you to enjoy the meal, not discover a second event waiting for you in the sink.

What happens to the leftovers?

When appropriate, leftovers can be packaged and left for you to enjoy later. Chris can discuss the best way to store and reheat anything worth saving—because excellent food should not meet an unnecessary ending.

Can you accommodate allergies or special diets?

Yes. Allergies, intolerances and dietary preferences should be discussed during the consultation. Chris can create thoughtful menus around many dietary needs so each guest feels considered and included.

Are private chef services only for special occasions?

Not at all. Romantic dinners and celebrations are wonderful, but so is a Tuesday when nobody wants to cook. Chris also creates family dinners, boutique dining experiences and meals simply because gathering around good food is reason enough.

Can the menu be completely customized?

Absolutely. Custom is the point. Chris can begin with your favorite foods, a specific ingredient, a memory, a cuisine you love, a dietary need, or simply what is looking exceptional and in season.
